batching_bug_found_and_fixed_this_repair: While browser-verifying the rewritten 3-cards-simultaneous UI with a rapid multi-click test (simulating several quick taps in succession, e.g. selecting multiple allergy members), discovered toggleCard/toggleMember read `groupUI[id]` from the component's render-scope closure instead of setGroupUI's functional-updater `prev` argument. Under React 18 automatic batching, several synchronous clicks fired in the same tick each computed their result from the same stale snapshot, so only the LAST click's toggle actually stuck -- a genuine state-loss bug, not the previously-documented harmless DOM-read-timing artifact. Fixed both functions to read from `prev[id]`. Re-verified with the exact same rapid-click reproduction: a 3-click batch (B/C/D) that previously would have dropped 2 of 3 now registers all 3 correctly, matching an earlier 5-click batch (A/B/C/D/F) that also now registers all 5 correctly. gameplay-qa-hotel-receive.mjs gained a permanent regression check for this pattern.
